items.title: Subdividing a path
items.gist: If every parameter has a neighborhood that the path sends into some member of a family of sets, then the path can be cut at finitely many increasing parameters running from zero to one so that each consecutive subpath has its range inside a single member.

items.title: A Lebesgue number
items.gist: For a compact subset K of Euclidean space and an open cover of K in its subspace topology, there is a positive radius such that every ball of that radius in K is contained in a single member of the cover.
items.departures: Specialize the linked pseudometric theorem to the metric subspace K, with s the whole of K and the family an open cover of K. Compactness of K supplies compactness of this whole space, and each open cover member is a neighborhood of its points. The balls are intrinsic to K, not ambient balls in Euclidean space. The applications need only K = [0,1] and K = [0,1]^2; they use the interiors of the preimages directly in those parameter spaces, as in Lean. The linked TauCeti neighborhood theorem is more general; the interval proof's Lebesgue-radius step links directly to Mathlib's open-cover lemma call.

items.title: Generation by a cover
items.gist: If every point of the space has some member of a family of subsets as a neighborhood, then the images of the functors induced by the inclusions of the members generate the whole fundamental groupoid as a subgroupoid.
items.departures: The members of the family are not assumed to be open and no connectedness is assumed of them or of their intersections; each member is only required to be a neighborhood of the points it covers. Generation by the fundamental groupoids of the cover members abbreviates generation by their inclusion images. This convention is limited to generation statements and arguments: the gluing domains remain the fundamental groupoids of the subspaces, since the inclusion functors need not be faithful.

items.title: The gluing functor
items.gist: Compatible functors out of the fundamental groupoids of the cover members extend uniquely to a functor F on the whole space, characterized by F composed with each inclusion-induced functor being F_i.
items.departures: The target is an arbitrary category, the members of the family are not assumed to be open, and neither they nor their intersections are assumed connected. The definition combines glue, its restriction equations, and eq_glue into the characterization of the unique extension. The two-subspace construction and its restriction lemmas are retained as source helpers; the text applies the general result directly to the cover {A, B}.

items.title: Generation by subspace groups
items.gist: If every point of the space has some member of a family of subsets as a neighborhood, every member contains the basepoint, and every intersection of two members is path connected, then the images of the fundamental groups of the members generate the fundamental group of the space.
items.departures: The members of the family are not assumed to be open, and path-connectedness is assumed of every intersection of two members, which for a member paired with itself is the member itself.

items.title: The descent homomorphism
items.gist: Homomorphisms to a monoid out of the fundamental groups of two subsets, whose interiors cover the space and which are path connected along with their intersection, and which agree after restriction to the fundamental group of the intersection, induce a homomorphism out of the fundamental group of the space.
items.departures: The target is only assumed to be a monoid, and the two subsets need not be open: only their interiors have to cover the space. Presented as a corollary of groupoid gluing (2.2) and the vertex-group functor construction (4.2); the proof checks compatibility using connecting paths chosen in the intersection.

items.departures: The target is only assumed to be a monoid, and the two subsets need not be open: only their interiors have to cover the space.

items.title: The based Seifert--van Kampen theorem
items.gist: If the interiors of two subsets cover the space, the two subsets and their intersection are path connected, and all three contain the basepoint, then the square of fundamental groups formed by the four homomorphisms induced by the inclusions is a pushout in the category of groups.
items.departures: The two subsets need not be open: only their interiors have to cover the space. The basepoint of the intersection is the basepoint of the space, which lies in the intersection because it lies in both subsets.
